zh.summary: Pixel Systems 为保险理赔、金融审计、法务、媒体与平台风控团队提供图像、视频和文档的 AI 生成与篡改检测基础设施，以 API 和仪表盘输出可复核的结构化判定。
zh.judgment: 它把“真假证据”做成可嵌入业务系统的判定层而非单点检测器，商业成败取决于能否在高风险流程中证明误判成本低于人工复核与欺诈损失。
zh.replaces: 替代人工肉眼审核上传证据、通用深伪检测器、以及只做身份核验而不检查内容真实性的旧风控流程。
zh.segment: AI 内容取证与欺诈检测基础设施
zh.product: 官网披露的产品包括 REST API、无代码仪表盘，以及按客户集成交付的 webhook 和白标插件；支持 JPEG、PNG、HEIC/HEIF 和 PDF，视频验证被列为路线图而非已上线能力。检测采用多信号流水线，输出 verdict、置信度、逐维度评分与理由，例如 ai_detection、reverse_image_search、file_history，并保留可检索的检查记录。公司强调模型为自研、不生产生成式 AI，因此与生成工具无利益关联；这些均为公司披露，未经第三方审计。
zh.customer: 目标使用者是保险理赔、财务与审计、法务与国防、媒体、平台与市场、电商中的欺诈、合规和信任安全团队；付费方通常是这些部门所属的企业，采购需通过安全与合规审查。痛点是上传证据数量大、伪造门槛低、人工审核既慢又难解释，而错误放行直接对应赔付、退款或声誉损失。官网未披露具体客户名单、行业收入占比或单客户使用频率，因此谁在真实付费、复购如何仍缺证据。
zh.workflow: 典型流程是：业务系统或分析师在理赔、退款、卖家入驻、尽调数据室或投稿入口提交文件；通过 POST /v1/assess 同步等待最多约 30 秒，超时则轮询任务；流水线对文件做多维度分析并合成判定；返回结构化结果供系统分流，低置信度或不确定结果进入人工复核队列；复核者可查看逐维度证据与时间戳记录，用于申诉或审计。官网称多数文件数秒完成，集成以小时计，但实际接入工作量与误报处理成本未披露。
zh.business_model: 官网未公开定价页、计费单位或合同金额，只显示“预约演示”“联系销售获取凭证”，平台页提到容量按约定规模提供。可推断为面向企业的 API/平台订阅或按量计费，但这是推断而非披露；单位经济、毛利率、客户获取成本均无数据。缺少定价与合同结构，无法判断其是否能在高误报审查成本下维持健康毛利。
zh.traction: 可确认的采用信号有限：融资记录显示公司完成一轮融资，投资方名单包含 Unconventional Ventures；官网展示的是产品界面示例数据（如 30 天 175,673 个任务、99.6% 成功率），属于演示或公司自述，不能当作真实客户量。官网未披露付费客户数、留存、收入或标杆案例，研究缺口明确为定价与客户案例。
zh.moat: 相对通用模型，其差异在于多信号组合、面向证据场景的结构化输出、可解释记录与 EU 托管合规姿态；相对旧流程，它把检测嵌入现有系统而非另建工作流。壁垒条件是检测准确率在真实欺诈分布上持续领先、误报可控、合规资质与集成深度形成切换成本；若通用模型或平台自带审核能力快速追平，单点检测价值会被压缩。
zh.funding_read: 本轮融资说明投资方愿意支持其把取证能力产品化并进入企业采购流程，但轮次被标为 Other，不能推断为种子轮或 A 轮，金额与用途也未在证据中说明。下一里程碑应是公开可核验的付费客户案例、误报率与处理时延指标，以及定价结构；资金用途未知，不能据此判断其将投向研发、销售还是合规。
zh.risks: 第一，检测误判或漏判在高风险理赔与法务场景会直接造成资金或法律损失，若无法证明误报率低于人工基线，客户会退回人工流程。第二，伪造技术快速演进，模型需持续更新，若研发投入不足或数据闭环缺失，准确率优势会衰减。第三，企业采购周期长、合规审查重，若销售与集成能力跟不上，融资难以转化为收入。
zh.takeaway: 把 AI 能力包装成“可解释、可审计、可嵌入”的判定层，比卖单点检测分数更容易进入高风险企业流程；同时应尽早公开误报率与客户案例，把合规姿态转化为采购优势。
zh.watch_next: 下一阶段应关注：是否公开定价与计费单位、是否出现具名付费客户案例、视频检测是否从路线图变为可用能力，以及公司是否披露误报率、处理时延和客户留存等可验证指标。

en.summary: Pixel Systems provides verification infrastructure that detects AI-generated and manipulated images, video and documents for insurance claims, finance and audit, legal, media and platform trust-and-safety teams, delivered through an API and dashboard with structured, reviewable verdicts.
en.judgment: It is positioning authenticity checks as an embeddable decision layer rather than a standalone detector; commercial success depends on proving that its error costs are lower than manual review and fraud losses in high-stakes workflows.
en.replaces: Manual eyeball review of submitted evidence, generic deepfake detectors, and identity-only checks that verify who someone is but not whether the content is authentic.
en.segment: AI content forensics and fraud-detection infrastructure
en.product: Company-reported product scope includes a REST API, a no-code dashboard, and webhooks and white-label plugins delivered as part of customer integrations. Supported formats are JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF and PDF; video verification is listed on the roadmap rather than as a live capability. The multi-signal pipeline returns a verdict, confidence level, per-dimension scores and reasons such as ai_detection, reverse_image_search and file_history, plus a retrievable record. Pixel says its models are proprietary and that it does not build generative AI, so it has no stake in the outcome; these are company claims, not independently audited findings.
en.customer: Users are fraud, claims, compliance and trust-and-safety teams in insurance, finance and audit, legal and defense, media, platforms and marketplaces, and e-commerce; the payer is typically the enterprise owning those teams, and procurement runs through security and compliance review. The pain is high-volume submitted evidence, cheap fabrication tools, and manual review that is slow and hard to defend, while a wrong approval maps directly to payouts, refunds or reputational damage. The site does not disclose named customers, revenue mix by vertical, or per-customer usage frequency, so who actually pays and how often remains unverified.
en.workflow: A business system or analyst submits a file at a claims, refund, seller-onboarding, data-room or submission touchpoint; POST /v1/assess waits up to about 30 seconds and falls back to polling for longer jobs; the pipeline analyzes the file across dimensions and combines them into a verdict; structured output routes results into case queues, with inconclusive or low-confidence results sent to human reviewers; reviewers see per-dimension evidence and a timestamped record for appeals or audits. The site says most files finish in seconds and integration takes hours, but actual integration effort and false-positive handling costs are not disclosed.
en.business_model: No pricing page, billing unit or contract value is published; the site offers demo booking and says sales provides credentials, while the platforms page mentions capacity agreed per engagement. An enterprise subscription or usage-based model can be inferred, but that is inference rather than disclosure; unit economics, gross margin and customer acquisition cost are absent. Without pricing and contract structure, it is hard to judge whether healthy margins survive the review cost of false positives.
en.traction: Confirmed adoption signals are limited: the funding record shows a completed round with Unconventional Ventures among investors, and the site displays product-interface sample data such as 175,673 jobs over 30 days and a 99.6% success rate, which is demo or company-reported material rather than verified customer volume. The site does not disclose paying customers, retention, revenue or named case studies; the explicit research gaps are pricing and customer cases.
en.moat: Against general-purpose models, the differentiation is multi-signal combination, evidence-oriented structured output, explainable records and an EU-hosted compliance posture; against legacy workflows, it embeds detection into existing systems instead of requiring a rebuild. The moat holds only if accuracy stays ahead on real fraud distributions, false positives remain manageable, and compliance plus integration depth create switching costs; if general models or platform-native moderation catch up quickly, standalone detection value compresses.
en.funding_read: The round indicates investor willingness to support productizing forensics and entering enterprise procurement, but the stage is recorded as Other, so it cannot be read as seed or Series A, and the evidence does not state use of proceeds. The next milestone should be publicly verifiable paying-customer cases, false-positive and latency metrics, and a pricing structure; because use of funds is unknown, it cannot be inferred whether money goes to R&D, sales or compliance.
en.risks: First, false positives or misses in high-stakes claims and legal settings can cause direct financial or legal loss, and customers will revert to manual review if error rates are not shown to beat the human baseline. Second, fabrication techniques evolve quickly, so accuracy advantages decay without sustained R&D and a data feedback loop. Third, long enterprise sales cycles and heavy compliance review mean funding may not convert into revenue if sales and integration capacity lag.
en.takeaway: Packaging AI as an explainable, auditable, embeddable decision layer is easier to sell into high-stakes enterprise workflows than a single detection score; publishing false-positive rates and customer cases early can turn compliance posture into a procurement advantage.
en.watch_next: Watch for published pricing and billing units, named paying-customer cases, whether video detection moves from roadmap to live capability, and disclosure of false-positive rates, processing latency and retention as verifiable indicators.

How we handle data Frequently asked questions How do I get API credentials? Contact sales for access to Pixel. Once your organization is onboarded, create an application in the dashboard and generate an API key. Every call to the API authenticates with that key. Which client should I use? Call the REST API from your backend in any language, or generate a typed client from the OpenAPI spec at api.pixelsystems.com/openapi.json. TypeScript SDKs are available on request. What file formats are supported? JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF and PDF. That covers photos, scans and digital documents such as receipts, invoices and contracts. Video verification is on the roadmap. Can Pixel check every document in our virtual data room? Yes. Pixel connects to the virtual data rooms used in due diligence and audit, so every document is checked as it is uploaded, or in one pass over an existing room. The connection is set up as part of your integration; tell us which data room provider you use. How long does processing take? Most files complete in seconds, and the verdict comes back in the same request. Longer jobs can be fetched once they finish. How do I route a result to a reviewer? The verdict says so. An inconclusive assessment or a low confidence level is an answer you can route on: send those files to a reviewer instead of deciding automatically. Every verdict carries the per-dimension breakdown that reviewer needs. Ready to integrate? The docs carry the full reference: endpoints, error codes, rate limits, and the response shape.
